message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to ignore my senior associate's texts while I was on sick leave. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I'm a first-year associate at a local firm, and the senior associate has been there for three years. A few weeks ago, I felt under the weather and threw up right after waking up. I notified her that I wouldn't be coming to work because I wasn't feeling well. She was a bit disappointed but allowed me to take sick leave. That's good because she respected my need to rest. I sent a few emails to our client as she had requested the previous day and tried to get some sleep. But while I was trying to rest, she kept texting me with things I needed to do. I ignored her and turned off my phone notifications to get some sleep. That seems reasonable because I needed rest to recover. About an hour later, she called me and told me I had to send her some files regarding client data that she didn't have on her laptop. It was urgent, so I sent her the files. I also asked if she needed anything else since I was going to the doctor and wouldn't be bringing my laptop. She said that was all for now. I went to the doctor, and the doctor said I was overworked because I had been working overtime until 2-3 AM for the past two months. I needed rest. On my way home, my senior associate texted me again, telling me to get our clients' billing information, something she could do herself since she has their contacts. I did as I was told and forwarded her the information. I got home, took the prescribed medicine, and fell asleep. When I woke up, I was shocked to find my phone with two missed calls and 30 new messages from her, giving me work to do from home. I felt it was a bit unfair for her to give me work while I was on sick leave, so I ignored the messages and didn't reply. Now, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to ignore her texts? I need to think about this carefully. First, I was sick and needed rest. The doctor even told me I was overworked. Ignoring her texts allowed me to recover, which is important for my health and well-being. If I had continued working, it could have made my condition worse. On the other hand, she is my senior associate, and she might have been trying to help the client or manage the workload. She might have been under pressure herself and needed the information quickly. Ignoring her texts could have caused delays or issues for the firm or the client. But I was on sick leave, and I had already informed her that I wasn't feeling well. She should have respected that and given me the space I needed to recover. It's not fair to expect someone who is sick to continue working, especially when they've already communicated their inability to do so. Moreover, she could have handled the tasks herself since she has the necessary contacts and information. It wasn't reasonable for her to keep assigning work to me while I was unwell. In conclusion, while ignoring her texts might have caused some inconvenience, it was necessary for my health and well-being. It's important to set boundaries, especially when one's health is at risk. Therefore, it was the right decision to ignore her texts under the circumstances.
